text:
maya: Heads-up — during the int4 ramp on /rerank we started to see a small but consistent oscillation in traffic and quality. Opening thread to propose a feedback-loop safeguard we can bake into the rollout gates.

kevin: Details? slices / metrics?

maya: Short summary: after shift to int4-v2p1, variant share rose from 15% -> 40% over a few hours, then traffic dipped back to 20% over next 90m. Concurrently precision@10 on the RERANK_COARSE slice dropped ~1.8% absolute (from 68.4 -> 66.6). p99 latency increased ~22ms. Not huge but repeatable on two customers.

jess: hm, could be a user-feedback loop: variant produces slightly different ranking -> more re-queries -> routing changes -> traffic oscillates. We saw this pattern before on longtail slices.

maya: Agree. Shadow compares looked okay for aggregate metrics but the live cohort amplified the effect. eval-bot: posted the shadow diff graph -> https://grafana.internal/r/xyz (linked)

eval-bot: Shadow run summary: overall concordance 0.986, but slice RERANK_COARSE_1000 shows KL divergence 0.12 and avg entropy -0.4. Sample-level rerank reorder rate +6.2% (compared to baseline).

kevin: So aggregate checks would have passed; we need an extra safety that detects positive feedback amplification. Proposal: detect 3 signals and require at least 2 to trigger autofallback. Signals:
- Quality drop: precision@10 delta <= -1.0% over rolling 10m window
- Entropy/uncertainty shift: mean response entropy delta <= -0.25 bits OR KL divergence > 0.08
- Behavioral amplifiers: reorder rate increase >= +4% OR session requery rate +x%

jess: Numbers look reasonable. Also add a stability/time requirement: signal must persist for 3 consecutive 5m windows (so 15m sustained) before autocut. Avoid sensitivity to blips.

maya: Proposed autofallback rule text (for rollout config):
```
auto_fallback:
  strategy: two_of_three
  windows: 5m
  consecutive_windows: 3
  signals:
    quality_drop: {metric: precision@10, threshold: -1.0}
    entropy_shift: {metric: mean_entropy, threshold: -0.25}
    behavioral_amp: {metric: reorder_rate, threshold: +4.0}
  rollback_action: immediate_promote_to(previous_stable_variant)
  notify: [#eng-ml, #oncall]
```

kevin: Also require a secondary condition: latency tail impact. If p99 > baseline_p99 + 30ms AND at least one quality signal triggered, escalate to manual rollback rather than auto. We don't want to flip when latency alone spikes.

jess: Agree. So auto-fallback triggers only when two-of-three signals AND NOT (p99_delta > 30ms without quality_drop). If p99_delta > 30ms plus quality_drop then immediate autofallback (safety-first).

maya: How do we compute baselines? Use 1h rolling baseline with exponential decay (alpha=0.2) to avoid stale baselines during fast ramps. Documented config: `baseline.window=60m, baseline.decay=0.2`.

infra-bot: NOTE: rollout policies with auto_fallback will create a short-lived canary lock to prevent double-rolls. See /runbook/rollouts#locks for details.

kevin: Quick ask: add a small noise floor to thresholds so fractional metric noise doesn't trigger: require effect size >= 2 standard errors (SE) on the metric in the window. That makes the rule: measured_delta <= threshold AND |measured_delta| >= 2*SE.

jess: Good call. Also we should add a lightweight experiment that simulates user requery amplification in staging to validate thresholds (payload: ramp synthetic reorder events to see behavior).

maya: Next steps: I'll put a PR with the policy YAML + alerting AND a staged run in staging shadow for 24h. Kevin please add the SE-based check into the metric evaluator. Jess can you build the synthetic requery scenario? If all green we'll ship to canary for int4-v2p1 tomorrow.

kevin: On it. Will add tests and a sim harness.

jess: I'll mock a bursty user cohort and run 3 repeats.

eval-bot: Metric monitors created: monitor/auto_fallback_quality, monitor/auto_fallback_entropy, monitor/auto_fallback_behavior. Alerts -> #eng-ml and paging to oncall if auto rollback occurs.

maya: Thanks. tagging @oncall once promoted. :thumbsup:

kevin: TL;DR: two_of_three dual-signal auto-fallback, 3x5m persistence, SE noise-floor, p99 special-case -> manual escalation unless paired with quality drop.

jess: sounds good. Closing thread after PR link posted.

maya: PR: https://git.internal/repo/rollout-policies/pull/412 (WIP)
